## 1. Welcome

Contributions are welcome: fixes, new components or adapters, documentation, feedback from use.

## 2. Setting up the environment

```bash
git clone https://github.com/flipova/foundation.git
cd foundation
npm install --no-package-lock --ignore-scripts
npm test
```

Prerequisites: Node.js 22 or later and npm.

## 3. Code organization

| **Folder** | **Contents** |
|-------------|-------------|
| `components/theme/` | Theme generated from the registries. |
| `components/contract/` | Types and recipes (pure functions). |
| `components/providers/` | Core of the providers, `rn-base/`, flipova, gluestack, reusables, paper, tamagui. |
| `components/ui/` | Unified components. |
| `design/` | XML registries, schema and tooling (`tools/`). |
| `scripts/` | Boundary checks between layers and consistency guards. |

## 4. Conventions

- Branches: one working branch per change; merge into main; a version is a tag (alpha, beta, rc, then stable on the same commit), see DOCS.md, sections 7 and 8.
- Commit messages: a short summary in the imperative mood, with details if useful.
- Code style and checks: `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run boundary`.
- Tests: `npm test` must pass; a new component adds its type, its recipe and its flipova implementation, then regenerates `COMPONENTS.md` with `npm run components:doc`.

## 5. Proposing a change

1. Open an issue or pick an existing one.
2. Create a working branch.
3. Open a pull request describing the change.
4. Pass the automatic checks (the `ci/ci.yml` contract, section 8, on Node 22) and the review.

## 6. Reporting a problem

State the version, the system, the steps to reproduce, the expected result and the actual result.

Issues: https://github.com/flipova/foundation/issues

## 7. License and conduct

Contributions are published under the project's license: MIT.

The repository's code of conduct (`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`) applies to all exchanges.

## 8. Continuous integration and delivery

The `.github/workflows/release.yml` pipeline is generated by Corral from the `ci/ci.yml` contract (`corral ci sync` after a change, `corral ci check` to verify; full reference: `ci/CI.md`). It depends on no private repository, so it does not need the ecosystem's `ORG_READ_TOKEN` token (FLP-ECO-001 of the `flipova.backend` repository).

| **Event** | **What runs** |
|---------------|----------------------|
| Pull request to `main` | model integrity, then `npm ci`, format, lint (including `design:check`, `design:verify`, `design:lint`), typecheck, `design:gen:check`, tests, build and `npm pack --dry-run`, audit, static analysis, secrets, CodeQL, dependency review. Node 22 |
| Tag `@flipova/foundation@X.Y.Z[-stade.N]` | the same checks, then publication to npm with provenance under the dist-tag `alpha`, `beta`, `rc` or `latest`, and creation of the GitHub release |

There is no publishing secret: publication uses npm trusted publishing, tied to the `release.yml` file and to the GitHub environment `production`. The repository reads no vault variable; the environment variables it knows (`FOUNDATION_DESIGN_DIR`, `FOUNDATION_PROJECT_ROOT`, `FLIPOVA_REQUIRE_DIST`, `UPDATE_COMPONENTS_DOC`, `CODEQL_FAIL_ON`) are tooling settings with no secret value. The documentation site is the `docs` step of `ci/ci.yml`: it is built on every pull request and published to GitHub Pages by `release.yml` after a stable delivery (there is no second workflow).
